about.title: Brentwood Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Brentwood has grown quickly, and with that growth comes busy shopping centers along Brentwood Boulevard, apartment communities off Balfour Road, and public spaces used by thousands of residents every day. When a property owner or manager fails to fix a spill, repair broken pavement, or light a stairwell properly, people get hurt. California premises liability law generally requires showing the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't address it in time. That's why documentation matters so much here: photos of the hazard, incident reports, and any store surveillance footage can disappear or get overwritten quickly. If you were injured on someone else's property in Brentwood, our team can review what happened and explain your options, at no cost to you unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Choose Us for Your Brentwood Fall Claim

items.title: Notice Is the Central Question
items.desc: California law generally requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. We can help gather evidence of how long the hazard existed.

items.title: Video and Records Vanish Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage from stores and complexes along corridors like Sand Creek Road or SR-4 is often overwritten within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be critical.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Bar, Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help present the facts fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Brentwood?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or park, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's best to have this reviewed as soon as possible after the fall.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means your compensation can be reduced by your percentage of responsibility rather than eliminated entirely. For example, being distracted while walking doesn't automatically bar a claim if the property owner also failed to address a known hazard. We can help sort out how fault might be allocated.

items.question: I fell at a Brentwood store on Brentwood Boulevard. What should I do first?
items.answer: Try to photograph the hazard before it's cleaned up, get names of any witnesses, and ask the store to preserve any surveillance video. Report the incident to management and get a copy of the report if possible. Then consider having the situation reviewed by our team before speaking further with any insurance representative.
